'''Liao Zhengyuan''' was a Saochian scholar and civil administrator credited with founding [[Kaonism]] during the [[Saochian Reorganization Period]].

== Work ==

Liao's best-known works were ''The Bond of People'' in 1844 and ''Measure of the Self-State'' in 1848. These texts argued for moralized governance, collective stewardship of essential resources, ritualized reform, and leadership restrained by public duty.

Liao rejected both aristocratic decay and violent populist revolt. His proposed "kaonic order" sought a disciplined social rhythm between law, labor, nature, and ethical statecraft.

== Suppression ==

During the [[Purge of 1865]], Kaonist and other alternative philosophies were banned. Liao was arrested and disappeared soon after. The source treats him as presumed to have died in exile.
